pairs.why: A shows the coffin from a raised three-quarter view with its lid top visible and resting on the grass like the real cards, while B is a flat upright front view with no top face and no ground contact.
A's rope coil and loop share one raised three-quarter view with the top of the coil visible, while B's ring reads nearly face-on against a side-on coil.
A shows the brim's top face from a raised camera like the real cap, while B is a lower view with steeper perspective that shows the brim's underside.
A's coil and ring share one tilted view and float without a ground plane like the real cards, while B adds a ground shadow and mixes side-on and face-on views.
A fills the frame with a flat frontal door and ivy at the edges like the real card, while B pulls back and shows a step and ground line that the real card lacks.
A is a raised three-quarter view with mild perspective and a chair that fills the frame like the real card, while B has wide-angle distortion, a tilted slab floor and a chair that leans.
A's raised camera, large hero and visible plank floor are slightly closer to the real cards, but both are similar and the difference is small.
B has a higher camera, shows more of the table top and fills more of the frame, closer to the real card's high view, while A's low horizon and small hero are farther away.
